sources.title: David R. M. Beck, “American Indian Higher Education before 1974: From Colonization to Self-Determination” (1995), 22, 24 n. 34.
sources.citation: David R. M. Beck, “American Indian Higher Education before 1974: From Colonization to Self-Determination,” in Critical Issues in American Indian Higher Education (Chicago: NAES College, 1995), 16–24, especially 22 and 24 n. 34; ERIC ED388478.

verification.note: Fresh selected text pp. 22–24 and note 34 read in the institutional publication’s ERIC scan; pp. 22 and 24 visually checked. Beck explicitly identifies Deloria as a 1965 guest speaker and workshop critic, citing Dorothy Parker’s 1992 biography p. 195. This is a named scholarly account, not fresh reading of Deloria’s original criticism or Parker’s book. The author’s broad first-Indian-history priority claim is not adopted.

sources.title: Douglas Miller, “Burying the (Uncle) Tomahawk,” Transmotion 2, nos. 1–2 (2016): 168–172.
sources.citation: Douglas Miller, “Burying the (Uncle) Tomahawk,” review of Laura Cornelius Kellogg: Our Democracy and the American Indian and Other Works and Clyde Warrior: Tradition, Community, and Red Power, Transmotion 2, nos. 1–2 (2016): 168–172, especially 169–170.

verification.note: Fresh selected scholarly review pp. 168–170 read in mirrored journal PDF; p. 169 visually checked. Miller describes an ideological gulf involving McNickle and Deloria, but contests an overly dismissive reading of McNickle’s reform program. Contextual corroboration only: the detailed workshop criticism comes from Beck. Neither reviewed book nor Deloria’s original statement freshly read; no endorsement of every reviewer claim is implied.
